questions.question: "Highway hypnosis" is a driving condition that can result from:

options.text: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
Taking frequent rest stops.
Getting too much sleep the night before.
Driving short trips on expressways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Staring at the road for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Highway hypnosis happens when you stare straight ahead without looking around. You stop checking the road ahead, behind, and to the sides. This causes you to zone out and makes you more likely to crash into traffic that slows or stops in front of you.

questions.question: Your vehicle is blocking traffic after an accident. You should:

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road, if possible.
Never move your vehicle.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your vehicle.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road, if possible.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if you can. Do not leave the scene without giving your information and offering help.

questions.question: To avoid carbon monoxide poisoning, drivers should:

options.text: Have their exhaust system checked regularly for leaks.
Keep their car off when it is in a closed garage.
Close vents when driving closely behind another car.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide is a deadly, odorless gas. Signs of poisoning are sudden tiredness, yawning, dizziness, and nausea. Fresh air is the only treatment.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
Hazard flashers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: In fog, use your low beam headlights and fog lights if you have them. High beams point upward and bounce off fog back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

questions.question: Your ability to stop is affected by:

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your stopping ability. Slow down on poor roads to keep control of your vehicle. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, which has the right-of-way?

options.text: The car approaching from the right.
The car approaching from the left.
The car whose driver honks first.
The car traveling the fastest.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car approaching from the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection with no traffic control device, yield to the vehicle coming from your right.

questions.question: Your wheels slip off the edge of the road. You should:

options.text: Jerk the steering wheel to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.
Speed up and steer back gradually.
Brake hard and stop immediately.
Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the pavement at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently brake and slowly steer back onto the pavement at a safe speed.
questions.explanation: Keep the wheels off the pavement and slow down using gentle braking. When you reach a safe speed, slowly turn the steering wheel to return to the road. Do not sharply jerk the wheel back onto the pavement.

questions.question: The most common cause of traffic crashes is:

options.text: New drivers.
Human error.
Bad weather.
Bad roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Human error.
questions.explanation: Crashes often happen when drivers do not see other vehicles or do something unexpected. Communicate with other drivers to help prevent crashes.

questions.question: You see a sign that says "Reduced speed, 35 mph." This means:

options.text: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
The new 35 mph speed limit starts at the next sign.
You have plenty of time to slow down.
You should go 35 mph only in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: The new 35 mph speed limit starts at this sign.
questions.explanation: A reduced speed sign tells you that a new speed limit is beginning. The new limit takes effect at the sign.

questions.question: Which statement about winter driving is false?

options.text: Winter is the most difficult driving season.
Check antifreeze and windshield washer fluid during winter.
Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
Snow tires are best for winter driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.
questions.explanation: Do not use cruise control on snow, rain, fog, or other hazardous conditions. Winter is the hardest season to drive in and requires extra care. Check your antifreeze and windshield washer fluid often. Snow tires improve grip on slippery roads.

questions.question: What shape is a stop sign?

options.text: Rectangle
Square
Circle
Octagon

questions.correctAnswerText: Octagon
questions.explanation: Stop signs are always octagon-shaped (eight sides). This shape is used only for stop signs.

questions.question: When is it illegal to drive below the speed limit?

options.text: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
When in heavy traffic in a construction zone
Only when driving in rural areas
When driving under adverse weather conditions

questions.correctAnswerText: When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you block or disrupt normal traffic flow. You can receive a citation for driving too slowly.

questions.question: After stopping for a school bus that is unloading children, what should you do?

options.text: Do not proceed until the children wave to you
Watch for children walking along the side of the road
Accelerate quickly
Turn on your emergency flashers

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children walking along the side of the road
questions.explanation: After stopping for a school bus, watch carefully for children walking along the side of the road. Always drive slowly and carefully in areas with children.

questions.question: When should you not pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve
When school bus lights are flashing
When approaching an intersection
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Never pass another vehicle on a hill, curve, at an intersection, at a railroad crossing, on a bridge, or in a no passing zone. Do not pass a stopped school bus with flashing red lights unless you are on the opposite side of a divided road.

questions.question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle approaching, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you
Drive to the right side of the road and stop
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you
Merge into the right lane and continue driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive to the right side of the road and stop
questions.explanation: You must yield to any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren. Move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, continue through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and go for help
Lay down in your car and go to sleep
Walk into the road and signal other drivers
Stay in your car, where you are most likely to be found

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car, where you are most likely to be found
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your vehicle. You are more likely to be found if you remain with your car. It is unsafe to walk around in a snowstorm.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: You may make left turns
You may make U-turns
You may pass slow-moving traffic
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: You may make left turns
questions.explanation: This sign shows a center turn lane. You can use this lane only for making left turns. You cannot use it for passing or going straight.

questions.question: Which offense will cause an automatic license suspension?

options.text: Racing on a public roadway
Graffiti
Lending your license to another person
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: These offenses result in automatic license suspension: racing on a public road, graffiti, and lending your license to someone else.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Hunting area
State park
Deer crossing
Wildlife preserve

questions.correctAnswerText: Deer crossing
questions.explanation: This sign warns that deer cross the road in this area. Slow down, stay alert, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do?

options.text: Drive using your four-way flashers
Drive using your parking lights
Do not turn on any vehicle lights
Turn on your headlights

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on your headlights
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights at dusk and on overcast days. Use low beams when within 1,000 feet of an oncoming vehicle and within 500 feet of a vehicle ahead of you. Always use low beams in poor weather.

questions.question: You can drive in the HOV lane if:

options.text: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
You are driving slower than other traffic.
You are driving faster than other traffic.
You are trying to get somewhere quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your vehicle has two or more people in it.
questions.explanation: Some highways have a left lane just for vehicles with two or more people. These HOV (High Occupancy Vehicle) lanes are marked with signs and diamond shapes on the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs alert drivers to upcoming road conditions and dangers. They are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns drivers that the road ahead has low clearance.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Drive with caution and be ready to slow down.
Do not drive in this lane.
You must stop completely and let others go first.
Slow down, be ready to stop, and let other traffic pass if needed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down, be ready to stop, and let other traffic pass if needed.
questions.explanation: A triangular sign means you must yield. Slow down as you approach an intersection with this sign and be ready to stop. Let other vehicles, cyclists, or pedestrians pass safely before you go.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Use tires with the correct air pressure.
Replace tires that are worn or damaged.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your vehicle slides on water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding also makes hydroplaning more likely.

questions.question: When you are in a travel lane on the road:

options.text: You can stop to drop off passengers.
You can stop to check an address.
You can make a U-turn or back up if you miss a freeway entrance ramp.
Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not stop for any reason. Keep driving until you can safely leave the road.
questions.explanation: Never stop in a travel lane. Keep driving until you reach a safe place to pull off. If you miss your exit, do not back up. Go to the next exit or find a safe place to turn around.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. allowed.
Hill ahead.
Truck stop ahead.
No trucks allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: A fire engine is following your vehicle on a two-lane street without using emergency lights or sirens. You should:

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as fast as you can.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move far to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is behind you without sirens or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Drive normally.

questions.question: Which light tells you to slow down and be careful at an intersection?

options.text: A flashing yellow light
A flashing red light
A solid yellow light
A solid red light

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing yellow light
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means slow down, proceed carefully, and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To use a roundabout correctly, you should:

options.text: Stop inside the roundabout.
Yield to vehicles entering the roundabout.
Drive in a clockwise direction.
Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to vehicles already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: A roundabout is a circular intersection with traffic flowing counterclockwise around a center island. There are no traffic lights. Enter from the right and yield to traffic already inside. Follow the circle until you reach your exit.

questions.question: You are driving on a narrow road and meet an oncoming vehicle. You must:

options.text: Pull completely off the road and stop.
Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road space.
Demand that the other vehicle pull over.
Turn on your high beams so the other driver sees you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the oncoming vehicle at least half of the road space.
questions.explanation: On narrow roads, you must give vehicles coming toward you at least half of the road space. Both drivers need enough room to pass each other safely.
